h: Henry VIII's childhood home and the Courtaulds' party pad
p: Long before the cocktail parties, Eltham was a royal favourite. Henry VIII spent much of his childhood here, and for a time it was one of the most important royal palaces in England, big enough to host the court at Christmas. As Greenwich grew in favour, Eltham slowly fell out of use, and by the time the Courtaulds arrived in the 1930s, the great hall was being used as a barn.

Stephen Courtauld was quite a character: a keen mountaineer and a backer of the British film industry, while Virginia was famous for her style and her love of entertaining. They spared no expense, kitting the house out with features that were cutting edge at the time, like a centralised vacuum cleaning system and a built-in sound system. Mah-Jongg the lemur even had centrally heated quarters.

After the Courtaulds left in the 1940s, the army moved in and used the site for decades. English Heritage took over in the 1990s and has carefully restored the interiors, so what you see today is a labour of love.

Don't miss the fifteenth-century stone bridge over the moat on your way in; it's one of the oldest bits of the whole site. Keen photographers should look out for the views of the great hall from the gardens across the water.
If you're staying local, Severndroog Castle on Shooters Hill is a quirky eighteenth-century tower with sweeping views over London, and the woods around it make for a nice walk.
